title: The Alibi of Bellwether Lane
premise: Yara Ashgrove, archivist of St. Verity's Cathedral, receives two letters about the same unsolved death on Bellwether Lane: one from a stranger confessing to the murder of Yara's estranged aunt, and one promising that 'the third letter will name you.' As Yara digs into the locked crypt's sealed records and their aunt's contested inheritance, they gather an unlikely circle — a disgraced constable, a lockmaker's widow, and a runaway choirboy — who become the family Yara never had. The killer is revealed to be the cathedral's beloved canon, who murdered the aunt to bury evidence that he himself was the unclaimed heir switched at birth decades ago; his identity hinges on a baptismal register Yara alone can read. In the crypt's final confrontation, Yara traps him by forging a false register entry, and chooses to claim both the inheritance and the found family waiting for them above ground.
about_author: J. M. Amberdale is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing births, deaths, and the lies between them in northern England. Their debut novel was inspired by a locked archive drawer no one had opened since 1962.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Yara Ashgrove, cataloguing the cathedral's restricted crypt on a rain-lashed evening, opens two letters delivered hours apart: a confession to killing Edith Ashgrove on Bellwether Lane twenty years ago, and a taunt promising a third letter. Yara's POV. Emotional beat: dread sharpened by a strange thrill — someone finally sees them.

chapters.title: The Register That Lies
chapters.summary: Yara cross-checks the confession against the 1962 baptismal registers and finds a page razored out. Disgraced ex-constable Bram Hale arrives investigating leaked case files, suspicious of Yara himself. Yara's POV with a Bram interlude. Emotional beat: wary alliance formed over shared professional shame.

chapters.title: Bellwether Lane, Revisited
chapters.summary: Yara and Bram walk the aunt's old street; the lockmaker's widow, Odile Fenwick, reveals Edith was asking about a baby swapped at birth before she died. The runaway choirboy Pip is caught eavesdropping and bargains his way into the group. Yara's POV. Emotional beat: the first warmth of found family forming around grief.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: The group breaks protocol to search the sealed crypt and finds Edith's hidden tin: photographs, a christening gown, and a note naming 'the boy who isn't the boy.' Canon Merridew catches them but oddly lets them go. Yara's POV. Emotional beat: vertigo — the inheritance Yara expects may not be theirs at all.

chapters.title: The Third Letter Arrives
chapters.summary: As promised, a letter names Yara as the next target unless they destroy the tin. Pip recognizes the handwriting as clerical script. Bram's old rival on the force dismisses the threat, isolating them further. Yara's POV. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve; the found family formally pledges itself.

chapters.title: Odile's Locks, Odile's Lies
chapters.summary: Odile confesses her husband made the crypt's duplicate key for Edith — and that Edith paid him with money from an anonymous benefactor inside the cathedral. Suspicion fractures the group; Bram accuses Yara of staging everything. Rotating POV: Odile's chapter. Emotional beat: betrayal and the ache of doubting your chosen people.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Isn't the Boy
chapters.summary: Pip decodes Edith's marginalia: two infants baptized the same night in 1962, one recorded twice under different names. Yara realizes either they or the anonymous heir is the false Ashgrove. A near-miss attack in the archive stacks confirms the killer is watching. Yara's POV. Emotional beat: identity crisis — if the name is stolen, what remains?

chapters.title: Merridew's Sermon
chapters.summary: Canon Merridew preaches on legitimacy and belonging while Yara, listening, matches his turns of phrase to the letters' cadence. Afterward he privately offers Yara the archivist post for life — a bribe wrapped in kindness. Yara's POV. Emotional beat: horror and pity entwined as the mentor becomes the suspect.

chapters.title: The Forged Page
chapters.summary: Yara plants a forged register entry claiming the true 1962 record survives elsewhere, then lets Merridew see it. He takes the bait, luring them all to the crypt at midnight to burn it. Bram stations Odile and Pip at the exits. Yara's POV. Emotional beat: cold clarity — the archivist weaponizes the archive itself.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: In the crypt, Merridew confesses: he killed Edith to protect the stolen life he built, then moves to kill Yara — but the 'register' is a decoy and Bram takes him down. Weeks later, Yara claims Edith's estate, shares it with Odile, Bram, and Pip, and files the true record under a new heading: family. Yara's POV. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
